newsitem.title: FRANCE: Portugal can enter EMU if it wants to - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Portugal can enter EMU if it wants to - Chirac.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday that Portugal can take part in a single European currency from the start if it wants to.

"I don't want to interfere in the internal affairs of Portugal, but my conviction is that if it wants to, it can without doubt (enter EMU at the agreed-upon date)," Chirac told reporters after a lunch and meeting with Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres.
When asked under what conditions Portugal could join the single currency, Chirac said it would have to adhere to the terms of the Maastricht treaty.

"Exclusively by the letter of the treaty. All the signatories of the Maastricht treaty have the same right, exactly the same right, to enter EMU from the start on the condition naturally that they satisfy the necessary convergence criteria," Chirac said.

Earlier on Monday, in a newspaper interview, Guterres said any country meeting criteria for a single currency should be allowed to join, Financial daily Les Echos reported. He said it would be a violation of the Maastricht treaty to exclude Portugal from the launch of a single currency simply because it is a southern European country.
He also expressed confidence that Portugal would be able to meet criteria from the single currency on time.
